open_questions: Weak and Powerless (Thirteenth Step): the tab's verse puts four and five sixteenths in a row on the bass drum at 80. Whether he played it with a double pedal is not found; the song is left out of the style until it is.
His kits by year: a DW kit in a dark finish with Devo (Boston, 2008, photograph); the 2007 Guitar Center interview gives his set-up by band but not the makes for A Perfect Circle's records.
Which drummers he names as influences beyond Devo's Freedom of Choice: the sources read name none.
The Offspring's Splinter (2003) and Days Go By (2012): which tracks are his.
Mer de Noms' recording record lists him as sole drummer; the liner notes credit Tim Alexander on The Hollow (track 1).

identity.name: Josh Freese
home_scenes: Orange County punk; Los Angeles sessions
identity.summary: Session and touring drummer on more than 400 albums since 1986, and a member of the Vandals (since 1989), A Perfect Circle (1999-2012, and since 2024) and Devo (1996-2023). The son of Disneyland's bandleader, he was playing a Simmons kit at trade shows at twelve and recording with Dweezil Zappa at sixteen. Variety: 'the pristine reputation as one of the most in-demand session drummers in the business'; he calls himself 'the blue collar freelance drummer to the stars'. On record the parts are clean and exact, nearly free of ghost notes: A Perfect Circle's heavy 6/8 with a rimshot on 4, The Outsider's bass drum in dotted eighths and its chorus in 3/4, the Vandals' and the Offspring's punk time.

traditions.impact: His father Stan Freese led the Walt Disney World and Disneyland bands; some of his earliest memories are of marching with the Disneyland Band holding toy instruments.
He has said he learned to play drums thanks to Devo's Freedom of Choice (1980); he joined Devo in 1996.

formative_events.event: Began playing at eight, on a Yamaha kit his father had received through a promotional deal.
Signed to a Simmons endorsement at twelve after playing a sample kit at the NAMM Show; played with Polo, a teenage covers band, at Disneyland from 1985 to 1988.
Left high school to record with Dweezil Zappa (Confessions, 1991).

eras.label: The Vandals, Devo and Guns N' Roses
eras.context: Orange County punk with the Vandals; sessions from 1991; a reformed Devo from 1996; Guns N' Roses, 1997-99.
defining_traits: punk at 160 and over, the open hat in eighths
the snare on every beat over the bass drum on the "and"s

eras.label: A Perfect Circle, Nine Inch Nails and the Offspring

eras.label: Sessions and the Foo Fighters

swing.notes: Straight: every tab read writes even eighths and sixteenths.

dynamics.balance: The snare and the bass drum carry it; rimshots for the backbeat in A Perfect Circle; few ghost notes.

feel_profile.interaction: A part for each section, held, the change of part marking the arrangement; the bass drum with the riff.

hand_techniques.name: Rimshots for the backbeat
hand_techniques.description: Judith and 3 Libras' choruses: every backbeat a rimshot.

hand_techniques.name: A cross-stick on every eighth
hand_techniques.description: 3 Libras' first verse: the cross-stick on each eighth of the 6/8 under sixteenths on the hat.

hand_techniques.name: Punk time on the crash
hand_techniques.description: Hammerhead and You're Gonna Go Far, Kid: the crash in eighths, the snare on every "and".

hand_techniques.name: The toms in place of the hat
hand_techniques.description: The Outsider's second verse: both toms together on the "e" of 1 and the "a" of 2; the floor tom in eighths under Judith's second pre-chorus.

foot_techniques.name: The bass drum in dotted eighths
foot_techniques.description: The Outsider's verse: 1, the "a" of 1, the "and" of 2, the "e" and "a" of 3.

foot_techniques.name: The hat foot as the time
foot_techniques.description: You're Gonna Go Far, Kid's verses and the Vandals' intro: the hat foot on the beats or eighths, the bass drum on every beat.

coordination.notes: Meter changes inside a song (The Outsider: 4/4 verses, 3/4 choruses, a 6/8 last chorus); whether he used a double pedal on Weak and Powerless is not found.

devices.description: Orestes, under the guitar solo: the snare on every quarter of the 6/8 bar (1, 3 and 5), three against its two dotted quarters, crashes with it.
The Outsider's verse: the bass drum in dotted eighths across the 4/4 bar, three, three, three and two sixteenths, under a straight backbeat.

voice_language.hihat: Eighths, open on every eighth for a chorus; sixteenths with the eighths accented in a 6/8 verse; the foot alone in a punk intro.
voice_language.ride: Eighths or sixteenths for a bridge, the bell on the beats.
voice_language.snare: Rimshots on 4 of a 6/8, 2 and 4, every "and" in punk time, every beat for a punk chorus; a cross-stick on every eighth.
voice_language.kick: With the riff: dotted eighths, the "and"s of 2 and 3 in 6/8, every "and" under a punk chorus.
voice_language.toms: Fills down the toms; both toms together in place of the hat for a verse.
voice_language.cymbals: The crash in eighths for a chorus, crashes on both pulses of a 6/8 bar; splashes and a china on 4.

aesthetic: A Perfect Circle: big and close, rimshots, Alan Moulder's mixes
the Offspring with Bob Rock: tight and dry
sound_profile.cymbal_character: More cymbals with A Perfect Circle than anywhere else, he said in 2007.

sample_hints.alternative-rock: A tight, dry studio kit; a big room for the 6/8 choruses.

evidence.note: His set-up by band, from a 2007 Guitar Center interview quoted on Wikipedia: the Vandals a four-piece, A Perfect Circle two rack and two floor toms and a second snare.

signature_traits.label: Parts, not jams
signature_traits.description: A figure for each section, every note placed and almost none ghosted; the change of figure is the arrangement.

signature_traits.label: Heavy compound time and changing meters
signature_traits.description: A Perfect Circle in 6/8 with a rimshot on 4; The Outsider moving from 4/4 to 3/4 to 6/8.

signature_traits.label: Punk time
signature_traits.description: The snare on every "and" under the crash in eighths, or on every beat over the bass drum on the "and"s, at 150 to 165.

patterns.name: Judith: a heavy 6/8, a rimshot on 4
patterns.function: The intro and chorus: a crash on 1, the open hat on each eighth after it, a rimshot on 4, the bass drum on 1, the "and"s of 2 and 3, and 6.

patterns.name: 3 Libras: a cross-stick on every eighth
patterns.function: The first verse: sixteenths on the hat, a cross-stick on every eighth of the 6/8, the bass drum on 1, the "and" of 2, 4 and the "and" of 5.

patterns.name: Orestes: three against two under the solo
patterns.function: The snare on 1, 3 and 5 of the 6/8, three quarters across its two dotted quarters, the hat between, the bass drum on 1, the "and" of 2, 4, the "and" of 5 and 6.

patterns.name: The Outsider: the bass drum in dotted eighths
patterns.function: The verse: eighths on the hat, opened on the "and" of 4; the snare on 2 and 4; the bass drum on 1, the "a" of 1, the "and" of 2, the "e" and "a" of 3.

patterns.name: The Outsider: the chorus in 3/4
patterns.function: Eighths on the crash, the snare on 2 and the "and" of 3, the bass drum on 1, its "and", the "a" of 2 and the "e" of 3.

patterns.name: You're Gonna Go Far, Kid: the gallop on the high tom
patterns.function: The pre-chorus: the high tom in sixteenths on 1 and on the "a" of 2, the "e" of 3 and the "and" and "a" of 4; the snare on 2 and 4; the hat foot between.

patterns.name: Hammerhead: punk time on the crash
patterns.function: The chorus: the crash in eighths, the snare on every "and", the bass drum on 1, the "a" of 1, the "e" of 2 and of 3, and on 4.

patterns.name: My Girlfriend's Dead: the snare on every beat
patterns.function: The chorus: the open hat and the snare on every beat, the bass drum on every "and".
